title: Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program — Patient Cost Share by Tier
content:
The patient's share of each claim line on the Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program is set by the tier the program sits on, and the tier follows the coverage the program bills.

| Tier | Coinsurance | Copay per 30-day supply (USD) | Plan deductible applies first | Automatic crossover to a secondary coverage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Testing Supplies Self-Pay Program | 100 percent of the Larkfield cash price | 0.00 | No | No |
| Testing Supplies Commercial HMO Program | 0 percent | 35.00 | No | No |
| Testing Supplies Commercial PPO Program | 20 percent | 0.00 | Yes | No |
| Testing Supplies Medicare Advantage Program | 20 percent | 0.00 | No | No |
| Testing Supplies Original Medicare Program | 20 percent | 0.00 | Yes | Yes |
| Testing Supplies Medicaid Program | 0 percent | 0.00 | No | No |

**How each column reads**

- *Coinsurance* is an integer percent of the payer-allowed amount on each claim line, taken after any deductible. On the self-pay tier it is instead the share of the Larkfield cash price the customer pays.
- *Copay* is a flat amount the plan applies per 30-day supply on a claim line; 0.00 means the plan applies no copay. It informs the patient responsibility the customer can expect, which the payer's remittance confirms.
- *Deductible applies* states whether the plan's annual deductible applies to this product line before coinsurance. The deductible amount itself belongs to the payer and arrives on the remittance.
- *Automatic crossover* states whether the patient responsibility left by the primary payer is crossed over automatically to an in-effect secondary coverage before any patient statement.

**Illustration (hypothetical figures).** On a claim line with an allowed amount of 100.00 and no deductible part, a coinsurance of 20 percent is 20.00 and a coinsurance of 0 percent is nothing; a plan with a 35.00 copay per 30-day supply applies that copay instead. The remittance, not this table, fixes the amount actually posted.
